item.title: Dangerous road layout at Blackwall Lane slip road towards Silvertown Tunnel, 26th July
item.description:
I would like to report what I believe is a significant road safety issue at the slip road from Blackwall Lane onto the Blackwall Tunnel Southern Approach, near the entrance to the Silvertown Tunnel. The slip road is extremely short, leaving drivers with very little distance to merge safely across to the third lane in order to access the Silvertown Tunnel. During busy periods this manoeuvre is particularly difficult because traffic on the main carriageway is often travelling at or above the 30 mph speed limit, creating very few safe gaps to change lanes. As a result, drivers are forced to either make unsafe lane changes or miss the Silvertown Tunnel entrance altogether. This appears to be a road design issue rather than a driver behaviour issue. I would ask the council and the relevant highway authority to investigate this location and consider measures to improve safety, such as: * Installing traffic control measures (e.g. traffic signals or metering) to create safe opportunities for vehicles joining from the slip road. * Reviewing the lane layout and merge distance. * Considering an alternative or redesigned entrance to the Silvertown Tunnel that provides sufficient distance for vehicles to merge safely. I believe the current layout creates an unnecessary risk of side-swipe collisions and sudden braking, particularly for drivers unfamiliar with the area. I would appreciate this being investigated before a serious accident occurs.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 228, Tunnel Avenue, East Greenwich, Greater London
